Tracking water ingress in commercial buildings.

We connect the location and timing of a water report with relevant roof, façade, plumbing and air-conditioning details before defining the repair.

Start with conditions, not the stain alone.

A stain shows where a problem became visible. We use its timing, pattern and surrounding building information to plan the investigation. The first scope should explain what will be checked, what access is needed and how any opening-up or testing will be agreed before a repair is specified.

Rain, equipment drainage or condensation?

We ask when water first appeared, which rooms or surfaces were affected, whether it followed rain or equipment use and what had changed nearby. Earlier repairs, equipment servicing and photographs taken at different times help clarify the sequence.

The record distinguishes a single event from a recurring pattern. We also note whether water remains visible after the reported trigger has stopped. That history guides the inspection; it is not used by itself to assign a confirmed cause.

Compare water marks against wind-driven rain, fixture use and cooling. Check upstream junctions, outlets, supply pipes and condensate drains.

Start with when and where the mark changes. A stain that grows after wind-driven rain leads us towards roof and wall junctions. Drops below a running unit lead towards the tray or drain. Beads forming along a cold grille, particularly near an open door into humid air, suggest surface condensation. A room can feel cool while moisture still enters through frequently opened doors or lingers in a low-airflow store. We compare the zone with adjacent spaces and record patterns before selecting a repair.

Agree the investigation before opening up

Log whether the mark changed in rain, after fixture use or during cooling. Use timing and location to trace the water route before repairs.

  1. 01

    Inspect the relevant accessible areas

    We review the visible elements connected with the report and record what can be established without disturbing finishes or components.

  2. 02

    Set any further test or access scope

    Where the cause is concealed, we explain the proposed inspection, opening-up or test, the affected area and the associated protection or reinstatement.

  3. 03

    Use findings to define the repair

    The repair location, materials and extent follow the findings. Record repair boundaries and the next inspection points.

A dry surface alone does not confirm the source has been addressed.

Roofing & waterproofing ↗

Choose the repair for the installed system

Log changes in water marks against rain, fixture use and cooling operation to prioritise the inspection.

Waterproofing information from Sika illustrates that systems are selected for their substrate and application. We check the existing system, adjacent joints, preparation requirements and service conditions before defining a local treatment or wider replacement.

For plumbing or HVAC-related findings, relevant equipment details and maintenance records help define the task. We keep a routine maintenance action, a defective part and a building-finish repair as distinct items, even when they are coordinated in one visit.

Sequence the affected finish with the source work

Gyprock maintenance guidance distinguishes surface damage from more substantial board damage. We assess the actual affected material and supporting condition before setting the extent of patching, replacement and refinishing. Painting over the visible mark is only one possible finish task.

The agreed sequence allows for source treatment, the condition required for the next material and the areas needing protection. Room use, stock, equipment and shared access are included in that plan.

Once the source has been addressed, the next scope depends on what remains sound. A firm substrate and intact fixings may allow a local patch. Soft ceiling board or swollen cabinet edging can need replacement and a separate finishing visit. We record drying conditions, the protection needed for nearby stock or workstations and the finish to match.

Building & general maintenance ↗

Make the investigation and repair easy to follow

  • Quotation factors

    Access, height, concealed conditions, the test or opening-up scope, material compatibility, finish restoration and further attendance are identified where relevant.

  • Completion evidence

    We record the location, findings, work carried out and checks actually performed, with photographs relevant to the agreed scope.

  • Follow-up observation

    If observation under particular rain or operating conditions is needed, we record those conditions and the agreed next action with the original history.

Start with a clear enquiry

Send the property type, affected location, timing and any previous work. A view of the damaged area and its surroundings is useful. We use those details to organise the inspection scope and identify which building or service areas need to be included.

Compare water appearance with equipment operation. Inspect supply pipes and condensate drainage as separate work items.

Keep the repair decision separate from drying and finishes.

We label checks completed and the next conditions to observe before reinstating finishes or removing controls.

Common questions

Does a ceiling stain always mean a roof leak?
Compare timing and location with roof, plumbing, façade and condensate routes to establish the source.
What information defines the repair quotation?
We can define the initial investigation and access needed. Once the findings establish the relevant defect and extent, we set out the repair and any finish restoration as the next scope.
